quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What is the most common type of crash involving 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania?

options.text: Single vehicle crash or running off the road.
Being hit on the side on an interstate.
Driving backward on a side street.
Driving on the shoulder of a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single vehicle crash or running off the road.
questions.explanation: Single-vehicle crashes and running off the road are the most common crash types for 16-year-old drivers in Pennsylvania. Between 2009 and 2011, there were 2,293 such crashes that killed 45 people.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true about safe driving speed?

options.text: Safe speed depends on many different conditions.
Driving slowly is always the safest choice.
The speed limit is always a safe speed.
Speeding up is always dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe speed depends on many different conditions.
questions.explanation: Safe driving speed depends on many factors, including road conditions, visibility, and traffic flow. When conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can clearly see all tracks before going forward.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one of the tracks is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can clearly see all tracks before going forward.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move as soon as one train passes. Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks. Another train could be coming on a different track.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road with no bike lanes and a bicyclist is ahead. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Keep driving straight. It is the bicyclist's job to move out of your way.
Wait to pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space at normal speeds, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of bicyclists. Do not honk unexpectedly, as it can startle riders and cause crashes.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plans ahead of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans ahead of time.
questions.explanation: Signal early when passing so other drivers have time to see your plans and react safely.

questions.question: When parking on the roadway, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Park at an angle.
Keep your turn signal on.
Turn your lights on.

questions.explanation: Use your four-way flashers when parking on the roadway. Leave enough space for other vehicles to pass, and make sure your vehicle is visible from at least 500 feet away in both directions.

questions.question: When you plan to turn, when should you activate your turn signal?

options.text: Only if there are other drivers following you.
Just as your car's front reaches the intersection.
Three to four seconds before you reach the intersection.
Two car lengths before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three to four seconds before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal three to four seconds before you turn to give other drivers time to react and stay safe.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.
Large trucks make less noise.
Large trucks drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need much more space to stop. Other drivers should stay where the truck driver can see them and where they can see the road ahead clearly.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
The cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space needed to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and how much traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
Give pedestrians the right-of-way only when they have the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. Drivers must watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if the pedestrian is crossing where they should not.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ center line.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic going in both directions cannot cross the center line to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers:

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should move to the left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should move to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end soon. Drivers in the right lane need to move to the left lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle its own full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Give the motorcycle only half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle using the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle its own full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Motorcycles need a full lane width to be safe. Even if space seems tight, the motorcycle needs room to move and balance.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
Cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
Do not have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow showed. But first, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go much faster or slower than other cars. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but never go over the speed limit.
